fr: J'ai acheté la robe que j'ai vue en vitrine.
en: I bought the dress that I saw in the shop window.
ipa: ʒe a.ʃə.te la ʁɔb kə ʒe vy ɑ̃ vi.tʁin
notes: The past participle vue agrees with the feminine direct object robe that comes before the verb, so it takes an e even though it sounds identical to vu.

fr: Elle a mis ses chaussures blanches ce matin.
en: She put on her white shoes this morning.
ipa: ɛl a mi se ʃo.syʁ blɑ̃ʃ sə ma.tɛ̃
notes: Blanches ends in a pronounced ch sound before the silent e, clearly different from the masculine blanc, so listen for that final consonant.

fr: Nous avons trouvé les gants gris dans le tiroir.
en: We found the grey gloves in the drawer.
ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ tʁu.ve le.z‿ɡɑ̃ ɡʁi dɑ̃ lə ti.ʁwaʁ
notes: Les gants requires a z liaison sound before the vowel, easy to miss since gants alone starts with a silent letter.

fr: Il va acheter un manteau noir pour l'hiver.
en: He is going to buy a black coat for winter.
ipa: il va aʃ.te œ̃ mɑ̃.to nwaʁ puʁ li.vɛʁ
notes: Le before hiver must be elided to l'hiver since hiver starts with a vowel sound despite the silent h.

fr: As-tu vu où j'ai posé mon écharpe ?
en: Have you seen where I put my scarf?
ipa: a ty vy u ʒe po.ze mɔ̃.n‿e.ʃaʁp
notes: Où meaning where and ou meaning or sound identical, so only context tells you which spelling to write.

fr: Ma sœur a essayé la jupe qu'elle a achetée hier.
en: My sister tried on the skirt she bought yesterday.
ipa: ma sœʁ a e.se.je la ʒyp kɛl a aʃ.te jɛʁ
notes: Achetée takes an extra e because the preceding direct object jupe is feminine, even though it sounds just like acheté.

fr: On a rendu les vêtements trop petits au magasin.
en: We returned the clothes that were too small to the store.
ipa: ɔ̃.n‿a ʁɑ̃.dy le vɛt.mɑ̃ tʁo pə.ti o ma.ɡa.zɛ̃
notes: On a sounds exactly like ont, so only the subject pronoun on with a single verb tells you which spelling is correct.

fr: Ils ont acheté des chaussettes en laine pour le froid.
en: They bought wool socks for the cold.
ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃.t‿a.ʃə.te de ʃo.sɛt ɑ̃ lɛn puʁ lə fʁwa
notes: Ont here is the verb avoir, not the pronoun on, and it triggers a liaison t sound before acheté.

fr: Cette chemise blanche va très bien avec ton pantalon.
en: This white shirt goes very well with your pants.
ipa: sɛt ʃə.miz blɑ̃ʃ va tʁɛ bjɛ̃ a.vɛk tɔ̃ pɑ̃.ta.lɔ̃
notes: Pantalon has three nasal-looking syllables but only the final on is a true nasal vowel, so don't add a written n after every syllable.

fr: Je vais essayer ce pull avant de l'acheter.
en: I am going to try on this sweater before buying it.
ipa: ʒə vɛ e.se.je sə pyl a.vɑ̃ də laʃ.te
notes: De le acheter is impossible in French, the le must elide to l'acheter before the vowel sound.

fr: Le vendeur a demandé quelle taille je porte.
en: The salesman asked what size I wear.
ipa: lə vɑ̃.dœʁ a də.mɑ̃.de kɛl taj ʒə pɔʁt
notes: Quelle and quel sound the same, so only the feminine noun taille that follows tells you to write quelle with two ls.

fr: Nous avons acheté deux robes roses pour l'été.
en: We bought two pink dresses for the summer.
ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ aʃ.te dø ʁɔb ʁoz puʁ le.te
notes: Roses simply adds an s for the plural with no sound change, so the ear alone will not tell you it is plural.

fr: Il a oublié son écharpe grise au restaurant.
en: He forgot his grey scarf at the restaurant.
ipa: il a u.blje sɔ̃.n‿e.ʃaʁp ɡʁiz o ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃
notes: Restaurant ends in a nasal vowel with silent final letters, do not write a pronounced t or n at the end.

fr: Ces chaussures sont trop grandes pour moi.
en: These shoes are too big for me.
ipa: se ʃo.syʁ sɔ̃ tʁo ɡʁɑ̃d puʁ mwa
notes: Ces here is the demonstrative these, not the possessive ses, distinguishable only through the plural noun context.

fr: J'ai lavé mon jean neuf à l'eau froide.
en: I washed my new jeans in cold water.
ipa: ʒe la.ve mɔ̃ dʒin nœf a lo fʁwad
notes: À l'eau needs the elided article before the vowel of eau, writing a le eau would be wrong.

fr: Elle va porter sa nouvelle veste demain soir.
en: She is going to wear her new jacket tomorrow evening.
ipa: ɛl va pɔʁ.te sa nu.vɛl vɛst də.mɛ̃ swaʁ
notes: Nouvelle and veste both end in a silent e that is not pronounced but must still be written.

fr: Mon frère a acheté un short bleu pour les vacances.
en: My brother bought blue shorts for the vacation.
ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a aʃ.te œ̃ ʃɔʁt blø puʁ le va.kɑ̃s
notes: Vacances has a nasal an sound in the middle syllable that learners often mishear as a full en.

fr: Avez-vous vu mes gants noirs quelque part ?
en: Have you seen my black gloves anywhere?
ipa: a.ve.vu vy me ɡɑ̃ nwaʁ kɛl.kə paʁ
notes: The inverted question avez-vous requires a z liaison sound between avez and vous that a simple vous avez would not have.

fr: La vendeuse m'a donné une taille trop petite.
en: The saleswoman gave me a size that was too small.
ipa: la vɑ̃.døz ma dɔ.ne yn taj tʁo pə.tit
notes: Me a must contract to m'a before the vowel sound of the verb avoir.

fr: J'ai mis mon manteau parce qu'il fait froid dehors.
en: I put on my coat because it's cold outside.
ipa: ʒe mi mɔ̃ mɑ̃.to paʁs kil fɛ fʁwa də.ɔʁ
notes: Parce que il elides to parce qu'il before the vowel sound of il.

fr: Nous avons choisi les mêmes chaussures que toi.
en: We chose the same shoes as you.
ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʃwa.zi le mɛm ʃo.syʁ kə twa
notes: Mêmes keeps its circumflex accent even though the accent does not change the sound, a common spelling slip in dictée.

fr: Elle a acheté une ceinture en cuir marron.
en: She bought a brown leather belt.
ipa: ɛl a aʃ.te yn sɛ̃.tyʁ ɑ̃ kɥiʁ ma.ʁɔ̃
notes: Ceinture has an in nasal sound while marron ends in a different on nasal sound, do not confuse the two nasal vowels.

fr: Le pantalon gris te va mieux que le noir.
en: The grey pants suit you better than the black ones.
ipa: lə pɑ̃.ta.lɔ̃ ɡʁi tə va mjø kə lə nwaʁ
notes: Mieux is spelled with an eu that represents a single vowel sound, resist the urge to add extra letters.

fr: J'ai oublié où j'ai rangé mes bottes d'hiver.
en: I forgot where I put away my winter boots.
ipa: ʒe u.blje u ʒe ʁɑ̃.ʒe me bɔt di.vɛʁ
notes: Où with an accent means where, while ou without an accent means or, only the accent distinguishes them in writing.

fr: Ma mère m'a offert un joli foulard en soie.
en: My mother gave me a lovely silk scarf.
ipa: ma mɛʁ ma ɔ.fɛʁ œ̃ ʒɔ.li fu.laʁ ɑ̃ swa
notes: Me a elides to m'a before the vowel sound of offert, never write me a as two separate words here.

fr: Les enfants ont mis leurs bottes avant de sortir.
en: The children put on their boots before going out.
ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ɔ̃ mi lœʁ bɔt a.vɑ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ
notes: Ont is the verb avoir here, easily confused by ear with the pronoun on since both sound identical.

fr: Cette veste noire coûte plus cher que l'autre.
en: This black jacket costs more than the other one.
ipa: sɛt vɛst nwaʁ kut ply ʃɛʁ kə lotʁ
notes: Le autre must elide to l'autre before the vowel sound, writing them separately would be incorrect.

fr: Il a acheté une chemise blanche et une cravate bleue.
en: He bought a white shirt and a blue tie.
ipa: il a aʃ.te yn ʃə.miz blɑ̃ʃ e yn kʁa.vat blø
notes: Both blanche and bleue add a feminine ending to agree with the feminine nouns chemise and cravate.

fr: Nous irons au marché acheter des vêtements neufs.
en: We will go to the market to buy new clothes.
ipa: nu.z‿i.ʁɔ̃ o maʁ.ʃe aʃ.te de vɛt.mɑ̃ nœf
notes: Vêtements has a nasal en sound in its middle syllable that is easy to mishear as a simple e.

fr: J'ai essayé plusieurs tailles avant de trouver la bonne.
en: I tried several sizes before finding the right one.
ipa: ʒe e.se.je ply.zjœʁ taj a.vɑ̃ də tʁu.ve la bɔn
notes: Bonne doubles the n and adds a silent e to agree with the feminine noun taille it refers to.

fr: Ta chemise est tachée, il faut la laver.
en: Your shirt is stained, you need to wash it.
ipa: ta ʃə.miz ɛ ta.ʃe il fo la la.ve
notes: Tachée is a past participle used as an adjective and takes a feminine e to agree with chemise.

fr: Mon père a acheté des chaussures noires pour le travail.
en: My father bought black shoes for work.
ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a aʃ.te de ʃo.syʁ nwaʁ puʁ lə tʁa.vaj
notes: Noires adds a silent s for the plural agreement with chaussures, invisible to the ear but required in writing.

fr: Je porte souvent un pull gris en automne.
en: I often wear a grey sweater in autumn.
ipa: ʒə pɔʁt su.vɑ̃ œ̃ pyl ɡʁi ɑ̃.n‿o.tɔn
notes: En automne links with a nasal liaison n sound before the vowel of automne.

fr: Elle a acheté ces baskets blanches pour faire du sport.
en: She bought these white sneakers to do sports.
ipa: ɛl a aʃ.te se bas.kɛt blɑ̃ʃ puʁ fɛʁ dy spɔʁ
notes: Ces here is the plural demonstrative these, not the possessive ses, even though both are pronounced the same way.

fr: Nous avons rangé nos vêtements d'été dans l'armoire.
en: We put away our summer clothes in the wardrobe.
ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe no vɛt.mɑ̃ de.te dɑ̃ laʁ.mwaʁ
notes: Both de été and le armoire must elide to d'été and l'armoire before their vowel sounds.

fr: Le magasin va fermer dans une heure, dépêchons-nous.
en: The store is closing in an hour, let's hurry.
ipa: lə ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ va fɛʁ.me dɑ̃.z‿yn œʁ de.pɛ.ʃɔ̃ nu
notes: Dans une requires a z liaison sound linking the two words before the vowel of une.

fr: J'ai acheté la même veste que ma cousine.
en: I bought the same jacket as my cousin.
ipa: ʒe aʃ.te la mɛm vɛst kə ma ku.zin
notes: Même keeps its silent final e and circumflex accent even though neither changes the pronunciation.

fr: Il a mis un pantalon noir et une chemise blanche.
en: He wore black pants and a white shirt.
ipa: il a mi œ̃ pɑ̃.ta.lɔ̃ nwaʁ e yn ʃə.miz blɑ̃ʃ
notes: Noir stays masculine with pantalon while blanche takes the feminine ending with chemise, listen for the gender of each noun.

fr: As-tu acheté le sac ou les chaussures que tu voulais ?
en: Did you buy the bag or the shoes you wanted?
ipa: a ty aʃ.te lə sak u le ʃo.syʁ kə ty vu.lɛ
notes: Ou meaning or has no accent, unlike où meaning where, the only difference is visual not audible.

fr: Il faut que tu choisisses une taille plus grande.
en: You need to choose a bigger size.
ipa: il fo kə ty ʃwa.zis yn taj ply ɡʁɑ̃d
notes: The subjunctive choisisses adds an extra s sound compared to the indicative tu choisis, listen carefully for it.

fr: Je doute qu'elle porte cette jupe au bureau.
en: I doubt she'll wear this skirt to the office.
ipa: ʒə dut kɛl pɔʁt sɛt ʒyp o by.ʁo
notes: Que elle must elide to qu'elle before the vowel sound, never write the two words separately.

fr: C'est la veste que j'ai vue hier dans la boutique.
en: It's the jacket I saw yesterday in the shop.
ipa: sɛ la vɛst kə ʒe vy jɛʁ dɑ̃ la bu.tik
notes: Vue takes a feminine e because it agrees with veste, the direct object placed before the verb.

fr: Ces chaussures sont plus confortables que ses bottes.
en: These shoes are more comfortable than her boots.
ipa: se ʃo.syʁ sɔ̃ ply kɔ̃.fɔʁ.tabl kə se bɔt
notes: Ces and ses sound exactly alike, only the demonstrative versus possessive meaning tells you which spelling to use.

fr: Quelle taille fais-tu, et quel modèle préfères-tu ?
en: What size do you wear, and which style do you prefer?
ipa: kɛl taj fɛ ty e kɛl mɔ.dɛl pʁe.fɛʁ ty
notes: Quelle agrees with the feminine taille while quel stays masculine before modèle, even though both sound the same.

fr: Je ne pense pas que ce pull t'aille bien.
en: I don't think this sweater suits you well.
ipa: ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə pyl taj bjɛ̃
notes: Te aille contracts to t'aille before the vowel sound, and aille is the irregular subjunctive form of aller.

fr: Ils se sont trompés de taille en commandant leurs chaussures.
en: They got the size wrong when ordering their shoes.
ipa: il sə sɔ̃ tʁɔ̃.pe də taj ɑ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.dɑ̃ lœʁ ʃo.syʁ
notes: Se here is the reflexive pronoun attached to the verb, not the demonstrative ce, only the sentence structure tells them apart.

fr: Ce vendeur pense que ces couleurs se démodent vite.
en: This salesman thinks these colors go out of style quickly.
ipa: sə vɑ̃.dœʁ pɑ̃s kə se ku.lœʁ sə de.mɔd vit
notes: Ce introduces the noun vendeur while se is the reflexive pronoun before démodent, both sound identical.

fr: Bien qu'il fasse chaud, elle porte toujours un long manteau.
en: Even though it's hot, she always wears a long coat.
ipa: bjɛ̃ kil fas ʃo ɛl pɔʁt tu.ʒuʁ œ̃ lɔ̃ mɑ̃.to
notes: Bien que triggers the irregular subjunctive fasse instead of the indicative fait, a common exam listening trap.

fr: Les baskets qu'elle a achetées ne lui vont pas du tout.
en: The sneakers she bought don't fit her at all.
ipa: le bas.kɛt kɛl a aʃ.te nə lɥi vɔ̃ pa dy tu
notes: Achetées takes both a feminine and plural ending to agree with baskets, the preceding direct object.

fr: Il est possible que ces gants soient trop petits pour toi.
en: It's possible these gloves are too small for you.
ipa: i.lɛ pɔ.sibl kə se ɡɑ̃ swa tʁo pə.ti puʁ twa
notes: Soient is the subjunctive of être with a silent final ent, do not pronounce it as a separate syllable.

fr: Quel dommage que ce manteau ne soit plus disponible en noir !
en: What a shame this coat isn't available in black anymore!
ipa: kɛl dɔ.maʒ kə sə mɑ̃.to nə swa ply dis.pɔ.nibl ɑ̃ nwaʁ
notes: Soit is the subjunctive form of être and sounds different from the indicative est, listen for the diphthong.

fr: C'est étrange que ses chaussettes aient disparu dans la machine.
en: It's strange that his socks disappeared in the washing machine.
ipa: sɛ.tɛ.tʁɑ̃ʒ kə se ʃo.sɛt ɛ dis.pa.ʁy dɑ̃ la ma.ʃin
notes: Aient is the subjunctive of avoir and is pronounced just like the indicative ont, only the grammar tells you which to write.

fr: Je préférerais que tu mettes une tenue plus discrète.
en: I would prefer that you wear a more discreet outfit.
ipa: ʒə pʁe.fe.ʁə.ʁɛ kə ty mɛt yn tə.ny ply dis.kʁɛt
notes: Mettes is the subjunctive form, spelled with a silent final s that adds no sound after the t.

fr: Ce sont les mêmes chaussures que celles de sa sœur.
en: These are the same shoes as his sister's.
ipa: sə sɔ̃ le mɛm ʃo.syʁ kə sɛl də sa sœʁ
notes: Ce sont sounds like son but is actually the plural of c'est, watch the context to spell it correctly.

fr: Selon moi, cette écharpe s'accorde mal avec ton manteau.
en: In my opinion, this scarf doesn't match well with your coat.
ipa: sə.lɔ̃ mwa sɛt e.ʃaʁp sa.kɔʁd mal a.vɛk tɔ̃ mɑ̃.to
notes: Se accorde elides to s'accorde before the vowel sound, the reflexive pronoun cannot stand alone here.

fr: Je ne crois pas qu'il ait déjà repassé sa chemise.
en: I don't think he has already ironed his shirt.
ipa: ʒə nə kʁwa pa kil ɛ de.ʒa ʁə.pa.se sa ʃə.miz
notes: Ait is the subjunctive of avoir and sounds identical to est, only the sentence structure tells you which verb it is.

fr: Les robes qu'elle a essayées ne lui plaisaient pas vraiment.
en: The dresses she tried on didn't really please her.
ipa: le ʁɔb kɛl a e.se.je nə lɥi plɛ.zɛ pa vʁɛ.mɑ̃
notes: Essayées agrees in gender and number with robes, the preceding plural feminine direct object.

fr: À mon avis, il vaudrait mieux que tu rendes ce pantalon.
en: In my opinion, you should return these pants.
ipa: a mɔ̃.n‿a.vi il vo.dʁɛ mjø kə ty ʁɑ̃d sə pɑ̃.ta.lɔ̃
notes: Rendes is the subjunctive form with a silent final s, distinct in spelling from the indicative tu rends.

fr: Ses vêtements étaient si élégants qu'on l'a remarqué tout de suite.
en: His clothes were so elegant that people noticed him right away.
ipa: se vɛt.mɑ̃ e.tɛ si e.le.ɡɑ̃ kɔ̃ la ʁə.maʁ.ke tu də sɥit
notes: Qu'on l'a packs two elisions together, que on becomes qu'on and le a becomes l'a.

fr: Quoiqu'elle soit chère, cette veste en cuir vaut vraiment le prix.
en: Even though it's expensive, this leather jacket is really worth the price.
ipa: kwa.kɛl swa ʃɛʁ sɛt vɛst ɑ̃ kɥiʁ vo vʁɛ.mɑ̃ lə pʁi
notes: Quoique elides with elle to quoiqu'elle, and it triggers the subjunctive soit rather than the indicative est.

fr: C'est la styliste qui a choisi ces tissus pour la nouvelle collection.
en: It's the stylist who chose these fabrics for the new collection.
ipa: sɛ la sti.list ki a ʃwa.zi se ti.sy puʁ la nu.vɛl kɔ.lɛk.sjɔ̃
notes: Ces before tissus is the plural demonstrative these, not the possessive ses, though the two sound identical.

fr: Ils aimeraient que nous portions des uniformes plus confortables.
en: They would like us to wear more comfortable uniforms.
ipa: i.lɛ.mə.ʁɛ kə nu pɔʁ.tjɔ̃ de.z‿y.ni.fɔʁm ply kɔ̃.fɔʁ.tabl
notes: Portions is the subjunctive form, pronounced differently from the indicative portons because of the extra i sound.

fr: Cette teinture a coûté cher, mais elle en valait la peine.
en: This dye job cost a lot, but it was worth it.
ipa: sɛt tɛ̃.tyʁ a ku.te ʃɛʁ mɛ.z‿ɛl ɑ̃ va.lɛ la pɛn
notes: Teinture has a nasal in sound in its first syllable, distinct from the en nasal sound later in the sentence.

fr: Il semble que ce tissu se froisse facilement au lavage.
en: It seems this fabric wrinkles easily when washed.
ipa: il sɑ̃bl kə sə ti.sy sə fʁwas fa.sil.mɑ̃ o la.vaʒ
notes: Ce introduces the noun tissu while se is the reflexive pronoun before froisse, both spelled differently despite sounding the same.

fr: Ces sandales sont confortables, mais ses talons sont trop hauts.
en: These sandals are comfortable, but her heels are too high.
ipa: se sɑ̃.dal sɔ̃ kɔ̃.fɔʁ.tabl mɛ se ta.lɔ̃ sɔ̃ tʁo o
notes: Ces and ses are homophones, so only the demonstrative versus possessive sense distinguishes them in writing.

fr: Bien qu'elles soient démodées, ces bottes restent très pratiques.
en: Even though they're out of fashion, these boots remain very practical.
ipa: bjɛ̃ kɛl swa de.mɔ.de se bɔt ʁɛst tʁɛ pʁa.tik
notes: Démodées agrees in gender and number with bottes, adding both a feminine e and a plural s.

fr: On dirait que ce manteau lui va parfaitement.
en: It looks like this coat fits him perfectly.
ipa: ɔ̃ di.ʁɛ kə sə mɑ̃.to lɥi va paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃
notes: On dirait sounds close to ont, but only the singular pronoun on with a singular verb is correct here.

fr: Il faudrait que vous repassiez ces chemises avant la réunion.
en: You should iron these shirts before the meeting.
ipa: il fo.dʁɛ kə vu ʁə.pa.sje se ʃə.miz a.vɑ̃ la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
notes: Repassiez is the subjunctive form of the vous conjugation, with an added i sound not present in the indicative repassez.

fr: À son avis, cette coupe ne va pas du tout avec ses formes.
en: In her opinion, this cut doesn't suit her figure at all.
ipa: a sɔ̃.n‿a.vi sɛt kup nə va pa dy tu a.vɛk se fɔʁm
notes: Son avis uses the possessive adjective son, easily confused by ear with the verb form sont.

fr: Je trouve que ce style te va mieux que celui de l'année dernière.
en: I think this style suits you better than last year's.
ipa: ʒə tʁuv kə sə stil tə va mjø kə sə.lɥi də la.ne dɛʁ.njɛʁ
notes: De année elides to de l'année before the vowel sound, the article cannot stay as le in front of a vowel.
